clips.linkedin:
Hand AI your reviews and returns notes, and it ranks the reasons people don't buy.

We launched the Rider Panel today. In its first study, a made-up folding smart trainer sold to 26 of 500 simulated UK cyclists with reviews out at launch. Without them, 3 did. One agent said she didn't want to be the guinea pig.

If you run a challenger brand, the reasons people walk away are worth more than the sales number. Give AI your reviews and returns notes. It hands back a ranked table of objections with a quote for each, so you know what to fix first.

The podcast voices are AI-generated. Full episode and article at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/rider-panel-market-research-ai-cyclists/
clips.text: A brand we invented, Northfold, with a folding smart trainer at four hundred and ninety-nine pounds. It's quiet and folds flat. Then we ran the same season four times on the same five hundred agents, changing one thing each time. And the headline? With the big reviews out at launch, twenty-six of the five hundred bought it. With no independent reviews, three did. Three. Three. Of the twenty-three buyers it lost, twelve bought a Wahoo KICKR CORE two instead. One agent, Folasade, a project manager in Hackney, put it simply. Northfold looked interesting, but she didn't want to be the guinea pig. That's the line I'd put in front of any challenger brand's board.
